definition: Django Deployment is a core concept in Python Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Django Deployment is
theory.body: Django Deployment describes the methods and patterns used within Python Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Django Deployment is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Django Deployment matters
theory.body: Without Django Deployment, systems built with Python Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Django Deployment works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Django Deployment follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Django Deployment.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Django Deployment
theory.body: Django Deployment offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
